[MUQATIL:7:205-206/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | The angels are mentioned in response to Meccan unbelievers asking what the Merciful is and whether they should prostrate to what the Prophet commands, as in 25:60. | mentions 25:60
[MUQATIL:7:205-206/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Unlike the Meccan unbelievers, the angels are not arrogant about worshipping God; they glorify Him by remembering Him and prostrate by praying.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p176#6/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Those who are with the Lord are the angels.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p105/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Those who are with their Lord are the angels.
[TAB-FULL:v10p671/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Ṭabarī admonishes the listener not to disdain worship and identifies humble reverence as worship. | mentions 7:204
[TAB-FULL:v10p671/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The angels near God do not disdain submission and humble reverence to Him; this humility is worship.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Those who are with the Lord are the angels.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Their glorification declares God free of evil.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Although God is in the heavens and on earth, the angels are called near Him because they are near His mercy, favor, and beneficence. | mentions 6:3
[IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648#2/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi glosses their glorification as prayer.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The subject of inna is the angels.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r2] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq explains their being with God as nearness to His mercy; whatever is near His mercy is described as being with Him, while God is everywhere.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · غيره | reports | Another view places the angels where nothing is carried out except God's decree.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r4] NAHHAS, d. 338 · قيل | reports | A further view says they are God's messengers, as one speaks of an army being at the caliph's court.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r5] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | They glorify God and declare Him free of every evil.
[NAHHAS:v2p173/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Their prostration means humbling themselves, unlike people of disobedience.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r12] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | This is the first prostration of recitation in the Qur’an.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r13] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · كفار مكة | reports | Meccan disbelievers objected, “What is the Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command?”; God then revealed this verse. | mentions 25:60
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r14] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | If even the angels brought near submit with humility and longing, people are still more entitled to do so.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas and other exegetes identify those with their Lord as angels.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj explains being with God as nearness to His mercy and favor, not physical proximity.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل المعاني | reports | Other people of meaning call this an honorific attribution: the angels are associated with God through their distinguished rank and the place from which His commands issue.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | reports | Another explanation says the angels are described as with God because they are His messengers to humanity, like an army said to be with a ruler though scattered across lands.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The mention of the angels' humility answers arrogant humans: even those greater than a human do not disdain worshipping God.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Those near their Lord are the angels, close to God's mercy.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Despite their rank, the angels worship God; a being greater than a human does not disdain worshipping God.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Their glorification means declaring God free of evil.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The angels prostrate to God.
[JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | After the preceding command to recite and listen to the Quran, these verses explain the manner of remembrance and supplication. | mentions 7:204
[JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Istikbār is seeking great rank by refusing the truth; the form istifʿāl originally conveys seeking.
[JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Tasbīḥ is declaring God transcendent above attributes that cannot properly be ascribed to Him.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Those near their Lord are the angels, distinguished by merit and honor.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | لا يستكبرون means they do not act proudly.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | They declare God transcendent and remember Him, saying “Glory be to God.”
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أبو هريرة | reports | The Prophet says that when a person recites a prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping, saying the human obeyed and gains Paradise while he disobeyed and faces the Fire.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · ثوبان | reports | Thawban reports the Prophet saying each prostration to God raises a servant one degree and removes one sin.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Those near their Lord are the angels; ‘near’ means nearness in rank and closeness to God’s mercy and favor through their obedience and pursuit of His pleasure.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | They reserve worship exclusively for God and associate no one with Him, implicitly rebuking other morally responsible beings.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | A report from the Prophet promises that reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf will place a screen between the reciter and Iblīs on Judgment Day, with Adam interceding for the reciter.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | “Those who are with your Lord” refers to the angels.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Their being “with” God means rank, honor, and nearness in status, not physical location.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The angels are humble and persist in worship, glorification, and prostration.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A Prophetic report says the sky groans, rightly, because no space the size of a handspan is without a standing, bowing, or prostrating angel.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · النخعي | reports | Al-Nakhaʿī, in the book of al-Naqqāsh, says one may either bow or prostrate at this verse’s prostration marker.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن وغيره | reports | Those “at your Lord” are angels; despite their exalted standing, they worship and remember God, so humans should not be arrogant about worship.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | “At your Lord” honors the angels through attribution to God; it does not mean spatial proximity, since God is transcendent above place.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | An alternative explains the phrase as being in a place God has honored and under His sole rule, like soldiers said to be “at the prince” because they are under his authority.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj explains being “at God” as being close to His grace and favor.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r14] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The angels glorify God by declaring Him free of what does not befit Him.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r15] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Sujūd may mean humility, prayer, or prostration in prayer; al-Hasan gives the last explanation.
[TABRISI:7:205-206/r16] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | There is consensus that this is a recitation prostration and the first such sajda in the Quran; Abu Hanifa deems recitation prostration obligatory, while al-Shafi'i and the author's companions call it a confirmed sunnah.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Those who are near their Lord are the angels.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | They do not act arrogantly or exalt themselves.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | One explanation of their worship is obedience.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Another explanation of their worship is prayer and humility within it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | One explanation of their glorification is that they declare God free of evil.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Another explanation is that they say Subhan Allah.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Their prostration means that they pray.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | The verse was revealed after Meccan unbelievers asked whether they should prostrate as commanded; it points out that higher-ranking angels do not disdain God's worship.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r9] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · النبي | reports | Abu Hurayra reports that when a person recites a prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping: the person obeyed and earns Paradise, while Satan disobeyed and faces Hell.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After urging the Messenger to remember God, the verse

points to the angels’ constant worship: despite their honor, purity, and freedom from passions, they persist in obedience, so embodied humans have even greater reason to do so. | mentions 19:31, 15:99
[RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المشبهة | rejects | The anthropomorphists take “those who are with your Lord” to imply that God occupies a place and direction; Rāzī rejects this as impossible on the rational and transmitted proofs given under 7:54 and 10:3. | mentions 7:54, 10:3
[RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The phrase can mean divine favor and mercy rather than location, as in the divine report that God is with hearts broken for His sake; this “withness” is not spatial.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | “With your Lord” may mean nearness in honor: a minister is closer in rank to a ruler than a doorkeeper, even when the doorkeeper is physically nearer.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The wording also honors the angels by associating them with the honored abode where God placed them, the realm of lights, spirits, obedience, and blessings.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A further sense is that the angels are God’s messengers to creation, like a caliph’s army said to be “with” him although its members are spread across the land.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أبو بكر الأصم | reports | Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm uses the verse to argue that angels are superior to human beings: the Messenger is urged to worship by reference to the angels’ worship, which he says works only if they are superior.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The order puts glorification first because it is the heart’s knowledge and purification of God, then prostration as bodily action; this shows bodily worship branches from the heart’s acts.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The phrase restricts the angels’ prostration to God, raising an apparent conflict with their prostration to Adam; Rāzī cites al-Ghazālī’s view that only earthly angels prostrated, not the great heavenly angels. | mentions 15:30, 38:73
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another reconciliation is that the verse’s statement is general while the command to prostrate to Adam is particular, and the particular takes precedence over the general. | mentions 15:30, 38:73
[RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī links the verse to other descriptions of angels continually standing in worship and surrounding the Throne while praising God. | mentions 37:165, 37:166, 39:75
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abū Ḥanīfah holds recitation prostration obligatory, citing the unqualified command, reports about Satan weeping when Adam’s child prostrates and about Paradise and Hell, and the Prophet’s practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجمهور | reports | The majority do not require salām after recitation prostration, while a group of early authorities and Isḥāq require it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عمر | reports | Al-Qurṭubī relies on the sound report that ʿUmar prostrated after reciting a sajdah, then later said God had not made it obligatory unless people chose.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | ʿUmar’s statement before the Companions, without objection, establishes consensus that recitation prostration is not obligatory.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The report that Adam’s child was commanded to prostrate refers to an obligatory prostration; the Prophet’s regular practice indicates recommendation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Recitation prostration requires prayer’s conditions: purity, intention, qibla, and a permissible time; Ibn ʿUmar and al-Shaʿbī are reported to allow it without purity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عمر | reports | Al-Bukhārī reports Ibn ʿUmar prostrating without purity; Ibn al-Mundhir reports the same of al-Shaʿbī.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق | reports | Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq require takbīr and raising the hands for prostration.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عمر | reports | A report from Ibn ʿUmar says the Prophet said takbīr when prostrating and rising.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | Mālik’s well-known position is takbīr on lowering and rising inside prayer; views differ on takbīr outside prayer, though most jurists require it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | prefers | Ibn al-ʿArabī prefers requiring salām: an act with takbīr should have an exit like prayer; this is even more fitting than for funeral prayer.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | Mālik’s well-known position forbids recitation prostration in obligatory prayer, whether quiet or aloud and alone or in a congregation, as an extra prostration.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | Another explanation is fear of confusing the congregation; on this rationale it is allowed alone or where confusion is unlikely.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو رافع | reports | Al-Bukhārī alone reports Abū Rāfiʿ praying ʿIshāʾ with Abū Hurayrah, who prostrated at al-Inshiqāq and said he had done so behind the Prophet and would continue until meeting him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عمران بن حصين | reports | ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn’s answer about a person who hears a prostration but was not seated for it implies the listener is not obliged to prostrate.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سلمان | reports | Salmān said, “We did not come for this,” regarding recitation prostration.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عثمان | reports | ʿUthmān held that prostration is due only from someone who listens attentively.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزهري | reports | Al-Zuhrī requires purity; at home face the qibla, while a mounted traveler may face any direction.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السائب | reports | Al-Sāʾib did not prostrate when a preacher prostrated.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي وجماعة | reports | Al-Shāfiʿī and a group allow prostration at any time because it is prayer for a specific cause.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | One view permits prostration until dawn brightens or until the sun yellows after ʿAṣr.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | Another view forbids prostration after both dawn and ʿAṣr.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | A further view allows it after dawn but not after ʿAṣr; these positions occur in the Mālikī school.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Timing opinions balance recitation prostration against the general ban on prayer after ʿAṣr and dawn, and differ on that ban’s rationale.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās transmits from the Prophet a supplication asking God to remove a burden, record reward, and store it as a treasure.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | In voluntary prayer, prostrate alone or in a congregation when disruption is not feared; the stated ruling permits prostration even if feared, though another view forbids that.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قيل | reports | A view says not to prostrate in voluntary congregational prayer when it may confuse the congregation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The angels are unanimously identified as those near their Lord.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن حبيب وابن وهب وإسحاق | reports | One count gives fifteen prostrations, from the end of al-Aʿrāf through the end of al-ʿAlaq; this is Ibn Ḥabīb, one report from Ibn Wahb, and Isḥāq’s view.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · بعض العلماء | reports | Some add the prostration at 15:98, making sixteen. | mentions 15:98
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن وهب | reports | Another report from Ibn Wahb counts fourteen, omitting the second al-Ḥajj prostration; this is the Ḥanafī position.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Al-Qurṭubī considers omitting the second al-Ḥajj prostration correct because the report establishing it is not sound.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عبد الله بن منين | reports | A report to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ says the Prophet taught fifteen prostrations, including three in al-Mufaṣṣal and two in al-Ḥajj; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq says Ibn Munayn is not a reliable proof.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عقبة بن عامر | reports | Abū Dāwūd reports ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir asking whether al-Ḥajj has two prostrations; the Prophet says yes, but Ibn Lahīʿah in its chain is very weak.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي | reports | Al-Shāfiʿī counts both al-Ḥajj prostrations and omits the prostration in Ṣād.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | The famous Mālikī count is eleven, omitting the last al-Ḥajj prostration and three in al-Mufaṣṣal; it is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r18] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو الدرداء | reports | Ibn Mājah reports Abū al-Dardāʾ saying he prostrated with the Prophet eleven times, listing al-Aʿrāf, al-Raʿd, al-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl, Maryam, one in al-Ḥajj, al-Furqān, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Ṣād, and one of the Ḥawāmīm.
[QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r19] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Another count attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās is ten, omitting the last al-Ḥajj prostration, Ṣād, and the three in al-Mufaṣṣal.
